intent: Add a test suite for rpi_nc_ca.sh (score 51), the third target in the hardest-first order, and add the two bind paths its suite exposed as missing from the shared jail_args. It stays on the allowlist at 98.63% as measured through run_all.sh, which is the invocation the gate itself uses.
scope: linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/features/lib/tests/test_rpi_nc_ca.sh: new, 26 assertions covering all 5 OS branches, both NSS stores and every Firefox outcome
Non-goal: no change to rpi_nc_ca.sh -- no latent bug surfaced
Non-goal: excluding heredoc bodies from the coverage denominator; that is the next piece of work and is what stands between this suite and 100%
changes: The five OS branches (Arch/Debian/RHEL/macOS/unknown) are selected by SEEDING the marker file each one tests for inside the jailed /etc, plus a `uname` stub for Darwin. Safe only because /etc is bind-mounted -- on a real host this would make the machine claim to be a different distribution.

The sshpass stub EMITS a certificate rather than recording the call. A record-only stub leaves an empty file and the subject dies on its own emptiness check, per the documented trap that a stub must materialise what the real tool produces.

SHARED-FILE BUG FIXED: the Debian branch does `mkdir -p /usr/local/share/ca-certificates`, and jail_args bound only /usr/local/bin. The suite aborted there under set -e. /usr/local/share and /etc/pki are now bound. Because jail_args is shared by every suite in the directory, all five libs were re-measured after the change (see verification) -- an over-aggressive mount looks exactly like unreachable code.

verification.evidence: rpi_nc_ca.sh: 72/73 = 98.63%, uncovered line 141, and no 'warn: case exited' -- every assertion passes. Measured through run_all.sh because that is the exact subject is_covered() builds; it is the gate's own view.

verification.command: same, but with the single test file as the subject
verification.evidence: 73/73 = 100.00%, reproduced twice. The runner reports 98.63% twice. Stable in both modes, so this is a kcov per-process merge artifact, not flakiness. Line 141 is the first line of show_help's heredoc BODY -- not a statement, so the denominator is wrong rather than the test missing.

verification.command: re-measure all five libs through run_all.sh after the jail_args change
verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh 39/39 = 100.00% (unchanged, and it is already off the allowlist so a regression here would make the gate unsatisfiable); rpi_nc_install.sh 11.36%, dwm_config.sh 47.95%, aw_autostart.sh 82.93% -- all unchanged. No mount masked anything.

verification.command: measure nc_php.sh with the OLD jail_args vs the NEW, single-file
verification.evidence: 84/85 = 98.82% under both -- no regression. Under the OLD args the RUNNER could not measure it at all (the suite exited 1 on the /usr/local/share abort this commit fixes); it now reports 'instrumented no lines' via the runner, a pre-existing merge artifact of the same family as line 141.

risks: jail_args is shared by every suite in the directory, so these two binds affect all of them. Mitigated by re-measuring all five libs; if a future bind does mask something, scope it to the leaf directory (--bind /usr/local/share/ca-certificates) rather than reverting the suite that needed it.

The suite seeds /etc/arch-release, /etc/debian_version and /etc/redhat-release. Run outside the jail this would make the host claim a false distribution, which is why the suite refuses to start when /etc is not writable.

98.63% vs 100% hinges on one heredoc-body line. Until shell_coverage_report.py excludes heredoc bodies from the denominator, any lib with a show_help-style heredoc is permanently capped below the bar.
rollback: git revert the commit; the suite disappears and jail_args loses the two binds, which returns the whole directory's runner to exiting 1 on the /usr/local/share abort.
After rollback, confirm the runner fails again for every suite in the directory -- that shared failure is the symptom this commit removes.
